narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Articulation Deck"**

Scope: this system governs the public landing page (`/`, `frontend/src/landing/`). The `/app` lip reader (`frontend/src/App.tsx`, `frontend/src/styles.css`: IBM Plex, uppercase labels, black with #ff3d00, light and dark tokens) is a separate, older system that was intentionally left as is. Do not reconcile the two, do not carry these tokens into `/app`, and do not pull the app's faces or colours into the landing page unless the user asks for that migration.

The landing page is a speech-language pathologist's deck of articulation cards laid on a cobalt table. Each card is die-cut from coated card stock with round corners and a punched ring hole; on it, a two-ink drawing of a mouth (upper lip in ink, lower lip in signal orange) becomes words in the patient's own voice. Proof sits on the top card: the real pipeline replay, the 96×96 model input clipped on as a small card of its own, and the real jawOpen trace. Concept screens of the planned phone app are drawn as articulation cards, never as phone frames.

The register is clinical-grade, not childlike: three inks only, Atkinson Hyperlegible for every word, its mono for every measurement, sentence case throughout, large confident 800-weight headlines with tight negative tracking. Density is low and sections breathe; the cobalt field and the orange field are the only full-bleed colour, with card stock and paper between them. Motion is the deck dealing: cards arrive fanned, and in the story section the top card slides off as you scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Three inks (cobalt, signal orange, ink) on card stock and paper; every tint is an alpha of one of those inks.
Die-cut cards (22px corners) with a punched ring hole, lifted off the table by a soft layered shadow.
The brand's two-bar mouth: ink above, orange below. Orange is the lower lip wherever it appears.
Words in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next; counts, clocks, values and footnote markers in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.
Sentence case, no tracking on labels; negative tracking only on 800-weight display.
The real jawOpen signal drives the mouth drawings and the replay graph; the motion is real speech without a face.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Cobalt, signal orange and ink, on card stock and paper. No fourth hue. A tint is an alpha of an ink (the graph area is cobalt at 14%, the clip window cobalt at 8%, the map's winning quadrant orange at 10%), never a new colour.

rules.name: The Lower Lip Rule
rules.body: Orange marks what is spoken, live or chosen: the lower lip, the underline, the active rule, the live state. Ink is the upper lip. When the two appear together, ink is on top and orange below.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Orange Rule
rules.body: Small text never sits in orange on stock (3.2:1), and text set on orange is ink (5.4:1). Card stock on orange is allowed only at display size.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Words are set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next; anything measured (a count, a time, a value, a size, a footnote number) is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase and no added letter-spacing on labels. Tracking only tightens, and only on 800-weight type at 25px and up.

rules.name: The Card Stock Rule
rules.body: Only cards cast shadows, and card stock stays opaque: a card leaving the stage moves out of frame before it fades.

rules.name: The Ring Hole Rule
rules.body: A card is a card because it has a punched hole. The hole shows the surface underneath (cobalt on the table, paper on the page, a deeper band tone inside a coloured band).

dos: Do build every surface from cobalt, signal orange and ink on card stock (#fbfaf7) and paper (#f0f0ed); make tints as alphas of those inks.
Do put the orange under things: the lower lip, a 0.12em underline beneath the key phrase, the active rule, the live state.
Do give every card 22px corners, a punched ring hole and the layered card shadow, and keep card stock opaque while it moves.
Do set measurements in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular figures, and words in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.
Do drive mouth motion from the real jawOpen trace, and hold a still frame under prefers-reduced-motion (the deal-in animation and smooth scrolling are also off).
Do draw concept screens of the phone app as articulation cards.
donts: Don't use faces as decoration; the only face on the page is the real clip inside the pipeline replay. Decoration is the mouth glyph or the mouth drawing.
Don't add a fourth hue, or set small text in orange on light stock.
Don't uppercase labels or add letter-spacing to them.
Don't draw the app inside a phone frame or beside the headline as a mockup.
Don't apply this system to `/app`, or bring IBM Plex, uppercase labels or #ff3d00 from `/app` into the landing page.
